title: Guide on How to Setup and Use the HighLevel MCP Server
snippet:
Connect your AI assistant to HighLevel so it can find CRM records and perform supported actions from your instructions. The HighLevel MCP Server, also called the LeadConnector MCP Server, connects through OAuth: sign in, choose the sub-account or sub-accounts to include, and approve the requested permissions.

MCP stands for Model Context Protocol. It gives AI assistants a standard way to discover and use tools from connected applications. With the HighLevel MCP Server, your assistant can work with supported CRM data and actions without you needing to know the underlying API.
The active catalog includes **more than 600 read, create, update, and delete operations across 38 domains**. The operations available to your connection depend on the OAuth scopes and permissions you approve.
---
## **Before You Connect**
You need access to the HighLevel sub-account or sub-accounts you want to connect and a supported AI client. ChatGPT users can find the official HighLevel plugin in Plugins. Muse and Grok Bot also offer officially listed apps. For custom MCP connections, use the corresponding URL below.
| AI client | Connection method |
|---|---|
| **Claude.ai, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork** | `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/anthropic/v2` |
| **ChatGPT, Codex, and other compatible OpenAI clients** | `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/openai/v2/` |
| **Cursor** | `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/cursor/v2` |
| **Muse** | Connect the official app in Muse; its OAuth endpoint is `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/muse/v2/` |
| **Grok Bot** | Add HighLevel from **Connect apps** |
| **ChatGPT** | Open ChatGPT → Plugins, search for HighLevel, and connect through OAuth. No manual MCP server URL is required. |
These connections use OAuth. During authorization, sign in to LeadConnector, select the available sub-account(s), and approve the requested scopes. All connection options use the current active LeadConnector MCP operation catalog.

## **How the Four MCP Tools Work**
The server exposes four unified tools. Your assistant uses these tools to find and run the operations available to your connection.
| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `list_locations` | Find the sub-accounts available to the connection, or return its single bound sub-account. |
| `search_operations` | Discover active operations for the task, including record searches and read, create, update, and delete actions. |
| `describe_operation` | Check an operation's inputs, example pay

title: HighLevel MCP Server Setup and Configuration Guide
snippet:
The HighLevel MCP (Model Context Protocol) Server provides a secure way for AI agents and MCP-compatible applications to interact with HighLevel tools and services. Using the MCP Server, AI assistants can retrieve records, update data, automate workflows, and execute actions directly inside HighLevel.
The MCP Server supports integrations across multiple HighLevel services, including contacts, conversations, calendars, opportunities, payments, and locations.
**Production MCP Endpoint**
```plaintext
https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/
```
---
## **Key Benefits of HighLevel MCP Server**
The MCP Server helps developers and AI builders create secure, scalable, and AI-powered workflows inside HighLevel.
- **Centralized AI Access:** Connect AI agents to multiple HighLevel services through a single MCP endpoint.
- **Secure Authentication:** Use Private Integration Tokens with scoped permissions for secure access.
- **Natural Language Automation:** Allow AI assistants to execute workflows using conversational prompts.
- **Multi-Service Connectivity:** Access contacts, conversations, opportunities, calendars, payments, and more.
- **MCP-Compatible Flexibility:** Connect with Cursor, Windsurf, OpenAI Playground, Claude-compatible clients, and custom MCP applications.
---
## **Supported MCP Clients**
The HighLevel MCP Server supports MCP-compatible applications that can connect through HTTP.
Supported clients include:
- Cursor
- Windsurf
- OpenAI Playground
- Claude-compatible MCP clients
- Custom MCP-compatible applications

## **Example MCP Workflows**
The MCP Server enables AI agents to perform actions inside HighLevel using natural language requests and MCP tool execution.
### **Common MCP Workflows**
- Searching contacts
- Updating opportunities
- Sending messages
- Retrieving calendar events
- Managing conversation history
- Accessing payment data

Cursor can connect directly to the HighLevel MCP Server using MCP configuration settings. Once connected, Cursor can discover tools, execute MCP actions, and interact with HighLevel using natural-language prompts.

MCP stands for Model Context Protocol. It is a standardized protocol that allows AI agents and copilots to securely interact with external tools and services.
**Q: What MCP clients are supported?**
Supported clients include Cursor, Windsurf, OpenAI Playground, Claude-compatible MCP clients, and custom MCP-compatible applications.

title: Connect MCP Servers to Conversation AI Bots | HighLevel
snippet:
Conversation AI bots can now connect to MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers to use external applications and tools during supported customer conversations. This allows bots to perform actions such as booking appointments through Cal.com, sending Stripe payment links, and updating Google Sheets without leaving the conversation. You can connect ready-made MCP servers from the Marketplace or add your own custom server. This guide covers connecting servers, configuring usage instructions, managing tool access, and monitoring MCP activity in Agent Logs.

MCP Servers Support allows prompt-based Conversation AI bots to connect with external applications and use their available tools while responding to customers. Instead of only providing information, a bot can perform supported actions in connected systems based on the customer's request and the instructions you configure.
Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides a standardized way for AI agents to interact with external tools and services.
For example, a Conversation AI bot can check appointment availability through Cal.com, create a booking, or use Stripe to send a payment link. It can also work with external applications such as Google Sheets and Notion, depending on the connected server and its available tools.
MCP tools work alongside existing Conversation AI capabilities, including Custom API actions, Knowledge Base retrieval, and Workflows.
---
## **Key Benefits of MCP Servers in Conversation AI**
MCP servers extend what Conversation AI bots can accomplish during customer conversations. By connecting external applications and configuring their available tools, you can support more tasks without creating a separate custom integration for every application.
- **Perform external actions:** Allow bots to complete supported tasks such as booking appointments, sending payment links, and updating external records during conversations.
- **Connect ready-made applications:** Choose from 40+ Marketplace MCP servers, including Stripe, Google Sheets, Google Calendar, Notion, and Zapier.
- **Connect custom tools:** Add your own MCP server using its name and HTTPS URL, with optional authentication credentials.
- **Control tool access:** Choose which tools each connected MCP server makes available to your Conversation AI bot.
- **Configure when tools are used:** Define the situations in which the bot should call each server and optionally specify what it should say afterward.
- **Monitor execution:** Review MCP tool calls

title: GitHub - basicmachines-co/open-ghl-mcp: An open source Model Context Protocol server for GoHighLevel API v2 with OAuth
snippet:
# GoHighLevel MCP Server
A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that provides seamless integration with the GoHighLevel API v2. This server enables AI assistants to interact with GoHighLevel's CRM functionality, starting with comprehensive contact management.
## Features
- 🔐 **OAuth 2.0 Authentication**: Full OAuth flow with automatic token management
- 🏢 **Agency or sub-account scope**: An agency (Company) token manages every sub-account via automatic agency→location token exchange; a sub-account (Location) token is used directly and is locked to that one sub-account
- 👥 **Curated domains**: Contacts, conversations & messaging, opportunities & pipelines, calendars & appointments, forms, custom fields & values, notes & tasks, users, and workflows — typed tools that handle API quirks
- 🌐 **Full-surface gateway**: `ghl_list_endpoints` + `ghl_request` reach the entire GoHighLevel v2 API (the long tail beyond the curated tools), with automatic token routing, quirk normalization, and confirmation gating on destructive/high-impact writes
- 🔄 **Automatic Token Refresh**: Handles token expiration seamlessly
- 🛠️ **MCP Tools & Resources**: Both tools and resources for flexible integration

Configuration
> **Basic Machines team members:** skip this — use the shared app credentials from 1Password and follow Team Setup instead of creating your own app.
For external/self-hosted use, create your own GoHighLevel Marketplace App:
1. Create your own GoHighLevel Marketplace App
2. Set the redirect URL to: `http://localhost:8080/oauth/callback`
3. Enable the scopes you want for the tools below (the server requests its full `ALL_SCOPES` set at authorization; the granted token is the intersection of that and the scopes your app enables)

#### 👥 Contact Management
| Tool | GoHighLevel Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `create_contact` | `POST /contacts` | Create a new contact |
| `update_contact` | `PUT /contacts/{id}` | Update existing contact |
| `delete_contact` | `DELETE /contacts/{id}` | Delete a contact |
| `get_contact` | `GET /contacts/{id}` | Get a single contact |
| `search_contacts` | `GET /contacts` | Search contacts with filters |
| `add_contact_tags` | `POST /contacts/{id}/tags` | Add tags to a contact |
| `remove_contact_tags` | `DELETE /contacts/{id}/tags` | Remove tags from a contact |

### 🔐 Authentication Requirements
All endpoints require proper authentication:
- **Company Token**: Used for location token exchange
- **Location Token**: Required for all

title: How to Use the HighLevel MCP Server
snippet:
This article will show you how to leverage the new GoHighLevel MCP (Model Context Protocol) server to empower your AI agents and copilots to access GoHighLevel data and tools seamlessly — all via a secure, standardized HTTP protocol.

The GoHighLevel MCP server is a standardized, secure protocol that allows AI agents to read and write data in GoHighLevel without needing SDKs or deep custom integrations. You can now give agents access to critical tools like Calendar, Contacts, Conversations, Opportunities, and Payments through a single, unified interface.
## Key Benefits of Using the MCP Server
Connecting your AI agents to GoHighLevel has never been easier or safer.
- Standardized Access: Query and update data through a unified protocol.
- Fast Integration: No SDKs required; works with any HTTP-supporting client.
- Secure: Uses private integration tokens (PITs) for granular, permission-based access.
- Scalable: Designed for future expansion to 250+ tools.
- Flexible: Supports popular clients like Cursor, Windsurf, and OpenAI Playground.

How To Set Up the MCP Server
### Step 1: Configure Your Agent/Client
Add the MCP endpoint and headers to your agent configuration:
json
CopyEdit
{
"mcpServers": {
"prod-ghl-mcp": {
"url": "https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/",
"headers": {
"Authorization": "Bearer <your-token>",
"locationId": "<sub-account-id>"
}
}
}
}
### Step 2: Get Your Private Integration Token (PIT)
1. Go to Settings → Private Integrations in your GoHighLevel location.
2. Click Create New Integration.
3. Select the required scopes (listed below).
4. Copy and securely store your token.
#### Required Scopes
Make sure your PIT includes:
- View/Edit Contacts
- View/Edit Conversations
- View/Edit Conversation Messages
- View/Edit Opportunities
- View Calendars & Calendar Events
- View Locations
- View Payment Orders & Transactions
- View Custom Fields
- View Forms
- Check Blog Post Slug
- Update Blog Post
- Create Blog Post
- View Blog Authors
- View Blog Categories
- blogspostsreadonly
- blogslistreadonly
- Create, Update and Delete Email Templates
- View Email Templates
- View Social Media Accounts
- View Social Media Statistics
- Edit Social Media Posts
- View Social Media Posts

- Individual MCP servers dedicated to specific services for targeted workflows.

title: Connect AI Clients to Project Management MCP | HighLevel
snippet:
HighLevel Project Management now connects with compatible AI assistants through Model Context Protocol (MCP), making it easier to organize and manage project work using natural language. With this integration, you can create and update tasks, subtasks, Spaces, and Lists without switching between your AI client and HighLevel. You can also work with custom statuses, custom field values, and task comments through an authorized connection. This guide covers how to connect a supported AI client using OAuth and start managing Project Management work through MCP.

Project Management MCP is an integration that connects compatible AI clients to HighLevel Project Management through Model Context Protocol (MCP). MCP allows an AI assistant to discover and use supported HighLevel operations through a standardized connection.
Instead of opening Project Management whenever you need to create tasks, organize Lists, or review comments, you can describe the action in your connected AI client.
The integration supports creating and managing tasks, subtasks, Spaces, and Lists. It also supports working with custom statuses, custom field values, and task comments.
Connections use a hosted MCP endpoint and OAuth authentication. You authorize the connection through your own account rather than configuring shared credentials or building directly against the Projects REST API.
**Supported AI Clients**
- Claude.ai
- ChatGPT
- Cursor
- Codex
- Claude Code
- Muse

- **Natural-language task management:** Create and update tasks, subtasks, Spaces, and Lists by describing the work you want to complete.
- **Less context switching:** Manage supported project activities without repeatedly opening the Project Management interface.
- **Custom statuses and fields:** Create tasks with appropriate statuses and custom field values, reducing manual adjustments after creation.
- **Task discussions:** Read task comments and post new comments through your connected AI client.
- **Simplified integration:** Use hosted MCP connectivity to work with supported project operations without building directly against the Projects REST API.
